issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: The engine revs up but the van is slow to pick up speed, shifts feel late or soft, or the van stops moving in Drive altogether. It often starts around 75,000 to 130,000 miles.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic (4T65-E) in these vans wears out internally. Worn clutches, a failing pressure control solenoid or overheated fluid let it slip until it can no longer hold a gear.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell; burnt-smelling or dark fluid is a bad sign. Avoid towing or hard acceleration and get a transmission shop to scan for codes before it fails completely.

issues.t: Harsh or jerky shifts
issues.sym: The van jolts when it shifts up or down, chatters pulling away from a stop, or the check engine light comes on with shifting that feels rough.
issues.why: GM issued service bulletins for harsh shifts on these vans, including one tied to the torque converter clutch solenoid (code P0742). Worn internal parts and old fluid make it worse.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A solenoid or valve body repair caught early can avoid a rebuild, so do not keep driving on a transmission that bangs into gear.

issues.t: Power sliding door reopens or will not latch
issues.sym: The power sliding door stops partway, reverses and opens by itself, will not close all the way, or does not latch. Some owners report it opening on its own.
issues.why: The door motor, cables, latch and the pinch sensors that tell the door to reverse wear out or go out of adjustment. A weak latch or a dirty track makes the door think something is in the way.
issues.next: Do not let children use the door until it is fixed. You can usually switch the door to manual mode while you wait. A shop can test the latch, cable and motor and adjust or replace the bad part.

issues.t: Coolant leak from engine gaskets
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping, you smell sweet antifreeze, or you see orange or green coolant on top of the engine or under the van. Left alone it can overheat the engine.
issues.why: The coolant crossover pipe and intake manifold gaskets on the 3.5L and 3.9L V6 harden and leak with age. GM has a service bulletin for replacing the crossover gaskets on both engines.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up with the correct Dex-Cool coolant and watch the temperature gauge. Get the leak fixed soon, since coolant getting into the oil can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm can crack (recall)
issues.sym: A squeak or clunk from the rear of the van over bumps. In the worst case the rear axle can partly come loose from the body.
issues.why: On some vans the rear trailing arm bushings wear early and the arm can crack or separate. GM recalled a batch of these vans (NHTSA 10V110000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls on the NHTSA or Chevrolet site. If a rear clunk shows up, have the rear suspension inspected right away.

issues.t: Alternator or charging system failure
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, lights flicker or dim, the battery keeps going dead, or the van sometimes will not start.
issues.why: Alternators on these vans fail with age, and weak batteries or corroded cable ends make the problem worse. Owners report charging problems across several model years.
issues.next: Have the battery and alternator tested; most parts stores do it for free. Replace whichever is bad and clean the cable ends.

issues.t: ABS, traction or StabiliTrak light comes on
issues.sym: The ABS, traction control or "Service StabiliTrak" light comes on, and the stability system may brake or cut power when it should not.
issues.why: A failing wheel speed sensor, a worn wheel hub with a built-in sensor, or a fault in the stability control sensors sets these lights. GM has a bulletin for various ABS codes on these vans.
issues.next: The regular brakes still work, but the safety systems may be off. Have the codes read to find which sensor is at fault.

issues.t: Will not start with "starter locked" message
issues.sym: Now and then the van will not crank and the dash shows a message such as "starter locked" or a security warning. It may start after waiting a few minutes.
issues.why: The anti-theft system is not recognizing the key or ignition switch, so it blocks the starter. Worn ignition switch parts or wiring faults are common causes.
issues.next: Try leaving the key on for about 10 minutes and then starting again. If it keeps happening, have a shop or dealer diagnose the theft deterrent system and ignition switch.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving or at idle. Some owners saw an "ignition disabled" message, and steering and brakes get heavy once the engine stops.
issues.why: There is no single cause. Reports point to the anti-theft and ignition system, a weak fuel pump (worse when the tank is low) and the engine computer.
issues.next: If it stalls, steer firmly to a safe place. Keep the tank above a quarter full and have the codes read soon after it happens so the cause can be found.

issues.t: Power steering goes stiff in wet weather
issues.sym: The steering suddenly gets heavy, especially in rain or puddles, and you may hear a squeal from the engine.
issues.why: The power steering pump is driven by the serpentine belt. A worn belt or a pulley with a bad bearing lets the belt slip when wet, so the pump stops helping.
issues.next: Have the belt, tensioner and idler pulleys checked. Replacing a worn belt and pulleys is usually the fix.

issues.t: Clunk or knock when turning the wheel
issues.sym: A clunk or knock you can feel in the steering wheel when turning, often at low speed or when parking.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for steering clunk and knock on these vans. Worn steering shaft joints and tie rod ends are common sources.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft, tie rods and front end checked. It is usually not urgent, but worn tie rods should be replaced.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or low fuel light stays on
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows empty with a full tank, swings around while parked, or the low fuel light stays on.
issues.why: The fuel level sensor in the tank wears out or loses contact, and GM issued several bulletins about inaccurate fuel gauges on these vans.
issues.next: Use your trip meter to track miles between fill-ups so you do not run out. A shop can test the sensor, which is part of the fuel pump module.

issues.t: Gasoline smell from cracked fuel line on tank
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell around the van that gets stronger over time, sometimes with fuel dripping near the rear.
issues.why: A plastic fuel line on top of the fuel tank module can crack and spray fuel. Mechanics report replacing several modules for the same crack.
issues.next: A fuel leak is a fire risk. Do not park in a garage and get the van inspected right away.

issues.t: Humming or grinding wheel bearing
issues.sym: A hum or grinding noise that rises with speed and may change when you turn. The ABS light may also come on.
issues.why: The front wheel hub bearings wear out. Owners filed many complaints about wheels and hubs on these vans.
issues.next: Have the wheel bearings checked. A badly worn bearing can get hot and fail, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Weak heat at idle
issues.sym: The heater blows warm air on the highway but goes lukewarm or cold when idling or in traffic.
issues.why: Usually low coolant or trapped air in the cooling system, often from a small leak. A partly blocked heater core does the same thing.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold. If it is low, find the leak and have the system filled and bled properly.

issues.t: Water on the floor from A/C drain
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the passenger side floor, often after running the A/C.
issues.why: The A/C drain tube that lets water drip out under the van gets clogged, so water backs up into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the drain tube cleared. Dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold and damage to wiring under the floor.

issues.t: Oil leak at oil pan or front crank seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the van or oil on the bottom of the engine.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for oil leaks at the front crankshaft seal and the side of the oil pan on these engines.
issues.next: Watch the oil level and add oil as needed. Have the leak source confirmed and the seal or gasket replaced.

issues.t: Brake pedal pulsation or vibration
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal shakes when you slow down, especially from highway speed.
issues.why: Warped or unevenly worn front rotors, which GM addressed in a bulletin about brake pulsation on these vans.
issues.next: Have the front brakes inspected. New pads and rotors usually fix it.

issues.t: Parking brake can slip (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake may not hold, or it may drag and make noise from the rear while driving.
issues.why: The parking brake lever on some early vans did not meet the federal standard, so the brake could slip or apply when it should not (NHTSA 05V287000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer repair is free.

issues.t: Rear seat latch can release in a side crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The concern is that a rear seat could come loose in a severe side impact.
issues.why: Rear seat latches on some 2005 vans could release too early in a side crash (NHTSA 05V061000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free dealer repair done.

issues.t: Rear wiper stops working
issues.sym: The rear wiper stops moving, moves slowly, or stops in the wrong spot.
issues.why: The rear wiper motor or its wiring in the liftgate fails.
issues.next: Check the fuse first. If the fuse is good, have the motor and liftgate wiring tested.

issues.t: Check engine light from gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with a message to check the gas cap.
issues.why: A loose, cracked or worn gas cap lets fuel vapor escape, which the emissions system reads as a leak.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on after a few days of driving, replace the cap or have the evap system tested.
